excerpt.rendered: Fifteen years and counting. Print, video, vehicle wraps, tradeshow booths, the lot. When they need something made, they call.

acf.fact_engagement: Ongoing client work – multiple projects per quarter
acf.brief_text: Innotech Windows and Doors is a high-end fenestration company building German-engineered products for commercial and residential use. This folder and its inserts are part of an ongoing brochure series I've been developing over several years. I built it as a presentation folder with custom business cards and other inserts, designed to give their customers a fuller picture of the product line.
acf.approach_text: I worked closely with the company's owner and the marketing team. I designed each part of the project as one cohesive marketing package, so every element was quickly recognizable as part of the Innotech family.
acf.outcome_text: The packet did its job – Innotech used it to win new clients.
acf.t_quote: We really appreciated David's attention to detail while building out many peripheral elements to our marketing portfolio.
acf.cta_heading: Need work that holds up for eighteen years?

excerpt.rendered: A hemp line that needed to look premium on a dispensary shelf. Identity, packaging, product photography, and a launch film.

acf.fact_role: Senior Designer, Brand Developer, Marketing Managment
acf.brief_text: ChenvreHemp was a sub-brand of the east west science health and beauty product line. I worked with Eastwest science to develop the brand design, the packaging development and the marketing campaigns. This was there venture into beauty and health using hemp as an ingredient in their product line.
acf.approach_text: We went through multiple variations of the idea, testing it with a number of focus groups before we launch this product. the intent is to create a solid high end brand that is accessible to everyone.
acf.outcome_text: East West Science was extremely pleased with the outcome of this branding, packaging and marketing work.
acf.t_quote: David's talents for brand creation, product development and marketing were greatly appreciated.

excerpt.rendered: An Innotech dealer that needed its own voice. A website and brand that borrow the quality cue without copying the parent.

acf.brief_text: Vindauga came to me in late 2024 to build a website for their window and door business – an extension of their construction company. They needed a high-end look to match the high-end fenestration they sell. At the time they were reselling Innotech doors and windows; they have since added other name-brand product lines.
acf.approach_text: I built the identity around the V – a letterform that doubles as a window frame and works as a mark on its own. Then I wrote the company's story and built the site around it, keeping the navigation simple and letting the product do the selling.
acf.outcome_text: They were happy enough with the site to bring me back for two more – Eberle Construction and First Light Fishing.

excerpt.rendered: A fishing charter in Prince Rupert run by two guys who know the water. Brand, website, and photography that makes a 4am start look worth it.

acf.brief_text: The client approached me with an urgent request to get online charter booking for a fishing company. There were a few unknowns but within a month and a half we had a system that gathered online payments, accepted multiple forms of payments, and looked better than most of the competition.
acf.approach_text: We assessed all the critical needs, sourced the right software and put into place the needed solutions to get things up and running as quickly as possible.

excerpt.rendered: Two decades of writing on justice and faith, finally organised. A dark, readable site built around his book reviews.

acf.tagline: Gospel as Counter-Narrative to Empire - Website Build
acf.brief_text: Wayne Northey approached me to build a website that would help him in his goal to use the Christian Gospel as Counter-Narrative to Empire. He has written extensively and also wanted to bring some of his thoughts to books that could be researched in this same effort.
acf.approach_text: I built a site that  holds his writings and book reviews - it has a well stocked book review database and it also is a launch pad for his writings on other platforms.
acf.outcome_text: He has quite a following and an extensive library of books that he has reviewed on his site.

acf.fact_role: Logo Design, Web Design, Print work, Some Photography
acf.brief_text:
Phoenix Ediger Sundecks is a Langley-based decking company with more than 30 years of experience. My work with Phoenix Ediger began nearly 18 years ago with updates to their existing website and soon expanded into a complete brand refresh, including a redesigned logo and a new website.

That first site served the company for approximately five years before we developed the current website and evolved the brand further. Over the years, our work together has expanded to include photography, drone video, printed forms, signage, and ongoing marketing materials—creating a consistent visual presence across both digital and physical touchpoints.
acf.approach_text:
My approach with Phoenix Ediger Sundecks has been to emphasize the qualities that set them apart: their approachable, client-focused service, commitment to quality, and attention to detail.

The brand and marketing have also been designed to communicate the depth of their experience and the range of services they offer—showing that they provide more than just a finished deck. They help guide clients through the process, recommend thoughtful options and enhancements, and create an experience built around trust, craftsmanship, and a strong client relationship.
acf.outcome_text:
Phoenix Ediger Sundecks continues to maintain a strong project schedule, completing work throughout the Lower Mainland—from Vancouver to Chilliwack. Their reputation has been built not only on the quality of their finished projects, but also on how they stand behind their work. When issues arise, they respond and work to make things right.

The team has been very positive about the evolution of the brand and the reach of their marketing. Over time, the combination of consistent branding, a strong web presence, photography, video, and supporting marketing materials has helped reinforce their reputation and keep Phoenix Ediger visible in a competitive market.

acf.brief_text: In 2017 the CEO of East West Science brought me on as Senior Creative Director and Designer. Over the next few years we built out a range of products, and Natural Pet Science was one I'm still proud of – a line of CBD products for pets. The whole idea sat on the line between whimsy and science: real formulation, delivered with a wink. The names said it all – Slim'Dog, Calm'Cat – and every package was made as distinct as the product inside it.
acf.approach_text: Each product was aimed at a different kind of pet, so I let the pet do the talking. The packaging spoke in the animal's own voice, asking for exactly what it wanted – the calm, the energy, the treat. That single move gave the whole line its personality: playful, direct, and a little cheeky, carried consistently from the packaging through the wider marketing.
acf.outcome_text: It landed well – the look drew a strong response in a crowded category. In the end the company chose to redirect its focus elsewhere, but the line stands as some of the most characterful packaging work I've done.

excerpt.rendered: A rack system with a sasquatch for a mascot. I took the joke seriously and built the video campaign around it.

acf.tagline: Serious steel, sold by a sasquatch.
acf.brief_text: Rack-On makes lightweight, high-strength mounting bars for garage and storage walls. The company already had a mascot – Racky the Sasquatch – and hired me to build a set of playful product videos around him.
acf.approach_text:
Racky delivers the rack, then takes it home and shows it off in his lair. Two settings, one joke, and a character who has to carry both.

We shot on location in Langley, BC, on a soundstage built as a cave. Piper Ediger performed as Racky and handled the stunt work, running the character through a range of setups until there was enough to cut.
acf.outcome_text: Rack-On came away with a library of short spots it can cut for social, retail, and its own site – and a mascot that reads the same in every one of them.
acf.t_quote: David's shoot helped bring to life this playful and fun side of our marketing.
